items.caption: This Shang-style form presents 馬 as a horse, with a prominent head and eye, flowing mane or tail, body, and legs.
items.alt: Black pictographic form with a large head and eye above an elongated body, with strokes suggesting mane or tail and legs.
items.selection_reason: Illustrates the whole-animal pictograph analysis and its recognizable horse features.

items.caption: This bronze-script form of 馬 retains the horse’s large eye, mane, body, tail, and legs in a more linear rendering.
items.alt: Black linear graph with a large eye in the head, strokes forming the body and mane, and descending leg-like strokes.
items.selection_reason: Adds a bronze-script example associated with a mid-Western Zhou vessel inscription, illustrating another attested form without implying a direct line of descent.

limitations.text: The sources support 馬 as a whole-animal pictograph, but the inspected textual account does not date the earliest individual inscription. The bronze image is a modern redraw associated with a vessel, not a photograph of the artifact.
